title: Cafe Bohemia opposite Miles Davis's quintet; Bohemia After Dark
summary: Dorham's band plays against Miles's band with Red Garland, Paul Chambers and Philly Joe, which scares them; the Dorham-Miles tension and the live album.

story.theme_name: Playing with and around Miles Davis
story.community_name: Playing with Miles Davis: joining, sessions and the band

blocks.x: So, and, and, but uh, we was working in the Cafe Bohemia , man, opposite the Power House--Miles Davis' band, you know the --
With Red and Philly Paul, man.* I never heard nothing like that in my life, man. I swear for a while, them dudes scared me to death. I didn't even want to get up on the stage.

Interesting thing, not to cut you off, but just to interject something--it's like I hear lot of the young people, especially since I been going around doing this lecture thing. If you talk about Miles Davis, then you talk about Miles' band with Herbie Hancock and Tony Williams., and Wayne Shorter. I tell them 'ya'll 'aint heard the Miles Davis band.' Miles Davis band--we had and Trane, Red, Paul and Philly Joe--well them guys used to scare you to death.
They scared--they, they, they scared, they scared, they scared us to death, man. I swear before God, man, they scared us. But uh, they be hitting it. They be hitting it man.
And uh, and at that time, uh, Coltrane was trying to get his stuff together. You know he--you know he didn't quite connect all of--all of it, you know.
*Red Garland, Paul Chambers and Philly Joe Jones, with John Coltrane, were members of the Miles Davis quintet, 1955-1956.

And guys would just sit and look at Coltrane, man, but just the rhythm section, man. A long--the rhythm section, man, those guys was fantastic, man. All three of those guys was fantastic soloists. Cause Paul was young and he was, he was talking like "I'm in New York, folks." You know, and he was on top of the beat of everything. And Philly Joe was--was talking like "I'm glad to have you," you know. And man that stuff was just something there all the time, you know. And Kenny Dorham and Miles they got--they had a thing going. They never--didn't like each other for some reason. And there was a thing going every night, you know. So we uh, our first--
--because they both play the same instrument?
Yeah. Playing the same instrument. But it was something that went back further than uh, you know, I, I understand it went back for years.
Well, anyway, so we did a live album called Bohemia After Dark.
From there. I don't know if you ever heard

It's--it was a pretty fair record, you know, I mean, it's fair and you know, the dudes is too scared to play, man. Cause, cause they know after you get through with your set, boy, you was going to be a catastrophe coming up in a minute. Them guys get on stage there, boy. You know, it look like they would be waiting for us. You know. Jesus Christ, man. I was glad when that stuff was over, man. When Miles left town, somebody would have gone out of here. And we--so I--then I left for the Jazz Prophets--after that I quit the band.
